column12: des
The universally practiced fist techniques and martial arts moves circulating in the martial world.
Fist strikes like a hammer, balancing hardness and softness in transitions and extensions, dismantling attacks from all directions. (Affected Attribute: Strength)
Utmost yang, utmost firmness, utmost dominance, utmost ferocity—its explosive power is swift and mighty, capable of shattering armor and splitting stone. (Affected Attribute: Balance)

The Great Harmony’s Righteous Method, the True Martial Tai Chi—this fist technique transcends sectarian biases, allowing anyone to practice it. The Tai Chi fist technique progresses from shallow to profound, using softness to overcome hardness. However, if one lacks sufficient insight and temperament, even a genius in fist techniques may fail to unleash its full might. (Affected Attribute: Inner Energy)

Rumored to be a divine martial art created by the former Prince Jingnan of the previous dynasty, none but those with peerless internal strength can hope to master it. If cultivated to perfection, one’s strikes unleash crisscrossing sword energy, capable of killing enemies from a hundred paces away. (Affected Attribute: Inner Energy)
The universally practiced single-handed light-blade martial arts moves circulating in the martial world.

Swift as a Lone Swan​​ – Graceful yet deadly, striking with precision, carrying the sorrow of a solitary swan. No need to ask the way home—parting with both gratitude and grudges, it pierces through armor for a thousand miles. (Affected Attribute: Agility)

​​Breeze Swift Sword​​ – Fast as the wind, formless and ethereal, its movements light and unrestrained. Rumored to be created by the wandering swordsman Jiang Huaichu, who later perished at the hands of the Imperial Guards, leaving the technique lost to time. (Affected Attribute: Agility)

​​Blade of the Horizon Pavilion​​ – A saber art passed down by the Horizon Pavilion, devised by its master, Zuo Sansi, while contemplating the ocean’s waves. Its force is sudden and violent, like the raging tides of the sea. (Affected Attribute: Strength)

​​Great Harmony Swordplay​​ – Said to embody the division of Yin and Yang, shaping the duality of existence, encompassing the vastness of the cosmos. The purest of Daoist sword arts, its depth and sophistication far surpass ordinary martial techniques. Yet, without sincerity and enlightenment, mastering its form is futile. (Affected Attribute: Inner Energy)

​​Drifting Duckweed Sword​​ – Gathering and scattering like floating duckweed, life and death as fleeting as foam. This sword art is said to have been created by an unknown eunuch of the previous dynasty—swift, elusive, and fierce, advancing and retreating like the wind. (Affected Attribute: Agility)

​​Crimson Plum Saber Technique​​ – A blade art forged by Yu Hongmei, merging the strengths of the Tianshan and Shaolin schools. Though brimming with baleful energy, it retains profound elegance. However, its overwhelming killing intent can lead the weak-willed astray into demonic paths. (Affected Attribute: Inner Energy)
​​Heavy-Blade Martial Arts​​ – Moves that seal and strike with the weight of a thousand jun.

​​Unsharpened Heavy Blade​​ – "The greatest skill seems unskilled." Known as Iron-Cleaver, it triumphs over finesse with simplicity—no need for flashy techniques, for the wielder and blade become one, and the body itself is the strike. (Affected Attribute: Strength)

​​Great Banner Army Saber​​ – A military saber technique passed down by the Great Banner Sect. Swift as lightning, fierce as a leaping tiger or soaring dragon—utterly domineering, its edge commands the surrender of ten thousand foes. (Affected Attribute: Strength)
​​Polearm Martial Arts​​ – Moves vast and sweeping, their terrifying might striking fear into all who witness them.

The spear techniques passed down through military formations involve blocking, thrusting, sweeping, and striking, advancing without retreat, with grand and unadorned movements. (Affects attribute: Agility)

There was the Xuanyuan Clan, whose dark blood entered the battlefield, patrolling the four directions, treading the eight wastelands to pacify the nine regions—this is the banner that commands reverence from all. (Affects attribute: Martial Power)
Hanging from the railings, extending and retracting, encircling and pointing, it clarifies the mind and releases the spirit, with Buddhist intent shining brightly. (Affects attribute: Physique)

Rumored to have been created by the Duke of Zhen, it dominates all directions, with spear shadows blotting out the sun, its momentum like a dragon emerging from the abyss, layer upon layer, or like silver serpents dancing wildly, impenetrable even to泼水. (Affects attribute: Agility)
A fan-based martial art circulating in the martial world, its techniques elegant and agile, yet also concealing lethal intent.

Echoing with mournful winds, obscuring vision with deceptive movements, the refined grace of scholars lightly expressed—this fan technique originates from the Tianya Haige, synthesizing the strengths of many schools, its forms faintly bearing the elegance of literary phoenixes. (Affects attribute: Internal Energy)

Two cycles of the sun and moon, a single sheet of paper halts the journey. This fan technique is gentle in motion, concealing internal force. The body twists and turns, its shadow flickering indistinctly. (Affects attribute: Internal Energy)
A concealed weapon martial art circulating in the martial world, its killing intent hidden within, utterly sinister and treacherous.
A concealed weapon martial art circulating in the martial world, its killing intent hidden within, utterly sinister and treacherous. (Affects attribute: Internal Energy)

After establishing the Great Snow Mountain Sect at Red Plum, observing the snowfall over the Heavenly Pool, this technique was created—its methods as unpredictable as an antelope’s horns, the trajectories of its concealed weapons extremely erratic and elusive, impossible to guard against. (Affects attribute: Internal Energy)
A common leg technique circulating in the martial world, its momentum fierce and unyielding.

Half-dreaming, half-awake, shattering delusions—laughing, drinking, singing wildly in drunkenness. Who knows the rarity of true understanding in this world? The peerless subduing of dragons, the unrestrained spirit of a national hero—this is how it should be! (Affects attribute: Martial Power)
A pair of geese flying over the river, feeding and moving together. Swift and fleeting, like geese skimming the heavens, leaving no trace, impossible to track. (Affects attribute: Martial Power)
A common dual-blade technique circulating in the martial world, vastly different from Central Plains martial arts.
It records the techniques of the Heartless Draw, distinct from Central Plains martial arts. Beyond this, no other origins of this technique can be traced. (Affects attribute: Martial Power)

Originally an Eastern swordsmanship, it spread to the Central Plains during the pirate rebellions, passed down orally until its true meaning gradually shifted, acquiring unique marvels. (Affects attribute: Martial Power)

A secret swordsmanship manual from an Eastern dojo, attacking where the enemy must defend, striking where they must falter—its techniques brim with killing intent, swift and straightforward. (Affects attribute: Martial Power)

A military blade technique passed down from anti-pirate garrisons along the coast, containing methods of dividing and converging attacks—precise, strict, and unadorned. (Affects attribute: Martial Power)
A rope-dart technique widely circulated in the martial world, its movements concealed and unpredictable, free to come and go, catching opponents off guard.
Flaming metal, shattering armor, sweeping and hammering—soft yet firm. (Affects attribute: Martial Power)
An archery technique passed down from military ranks, every movement imbued with a solemn killing intent.

It fully records the archery methods passed down through military formations, with mind and body techniques trained separately to achieve pinpoint accuracy, piercing stone and burying arrowheads. (Affects attribute: Martial Power)
Whip techniques are cunning and bizarre, rare in the martial world—those who master soft whips are invariably gifted individuals.

The snake, scorpion, toad, centipede, and spider are the five sacred scaled spirits. Combined with purified gu cultivation, this is the secret whip technique of the Five Saints Sect. (Affects attribute: Martial Power)

Created a century ago by a martial world eccentric, its techniques are fierce and graceful, its power like thunder—but those with insufficient internal energy who force themselves to learn it risk self-harm. (Affects attribute: Martial Power)
A firearm technique passed down from military ranks, moving like thunder.

A detailed manual on firearms and mechanisms imported from the Western Regions, containing methods for maintenance, firing, disassembly, and more—profound, obscure, and difficult to describe. (Affects attribute: Martial Power)
A common short-weapon technique in the martial world, excelling in close-quarters combat, seeking victory in danger.

A secret technique of the Five Saints Sect, specializing in close-quarters combat and lethal strikes. Observing its movements is like witnessing lovers’ sorrow—mysterious and inscrutable, yet vicious and treacherous to the extreme. (Affects attribute: Internal Energy)

As the waning moon departs, the beauty bids farewell with tears. Like the moon hidden by clouds, or clouds veiling the moon—its momentum like a sudden celestial brilliance, chilling enemies to the bone. (Affects attribute: Internal Energy)
Hybrid Martial Arts, freely combined.

An internal energy technique passed down by the Tianya Haige, rumored to have been left behind a century ago by an unnamed elder who passed by the Stone of Three Lives. Its techniques are vast and profound, infinitely subtle.
Derived from fragments of the Hetu and Luoshu, bizarre and grotesque, further tainted by cruelty and bloodlust—none who practice this art meet a good end.
Shattered treasures remain, unbroken jade endures; within it lies a heart method, strongest yet softest, of wondrous and infinite application.
It is said to be a cultivation method created by the Miao Ancestor in ancient times, its doctrines often run contrary to the Central Plains' ways, quite extraordinary.

In the fourth year of Shenshou, Dao Zu, after defecting from Shaolin at Red Plum, uniquely devised this method: virtuous yet prideful, taught yet unyielding, hearing the dharma yet unenlightened — such is an Asura.
The Question of Taishu remains unanswered, the healer's path walked alone; this chapter of the Lingshu, saving lives with medicine, is sufficient by itself.

The secret truth transmitted from Taihe Mountain distinguishes Qian from Kun, its simplicity reveals prosperity; the method progresses from shallow to deep, truly the orthodox school of the Profound Gate.

Comprehending the profound leads to enlightenment, understanding the principle allows grasping the covenant; this heart formula is ancient and difficult to discern, seemingly linked to the Kunlun Heavenly Pool.

Sucking stars, devouring the cosmos; consuming creation, burying dust; this style's tyranny crowns the world, far surpassing ordinary martial arts — yet its overwhelming power means only those of great perseverance can master it to the peak.
Tears of Xiang Fei stain the bamboo, flowing water buries orchids carelessly; this book holds knowledge that is martial arts, yet like poetry; its sorrowful intent defies further words.
A rare inner energy heart method, its operation like morning clouds filling the sky, covering fields and clouds; where purple qi reaches, all transformations vanish.
Orthodox Buddhist methods, vast and mighty; if unleashed with a roar, thunder rumbles, causing the enemy’s liver and gall to burst — collapsing without battle.
Two Zen Temples newly established, many styles spread; this heart method also emerged during the chaos of Shaolin's division, later vanishing into the Jianghu, ultimately fading from knowledge.

Dreams chill pass the immortal palace, spirit fuses merging with the Grand Void; said to be left behind by the Taihe Dao Ancestor at ascension, differing from many practices, demanding purity, nature, sudden enlightenment to ascend — only those of extraordinary insight can cultivate it.

Fierce hardness tempered by training, forging bone and refining blood; masters exude abundant, vigorous true qi flowing throughout their body — broken bones cause no pain, bathed in blood but do not die; fearless, thus undefeatable.
Said to be left behind by a healing sage of the previous dynasty; its recorded meridian theory is profound and abstruse — applying it to martial arts yields unique strengths.
Unique Miao heart method; masters captivate with a glance, unsettling minds without weapons — righteous or evil remains unknown.
Yao's ninth year, Zhi Qi wreaked havoc; Yinglong drove it to the foot of Huaiyang Mountain; its resentment shook mountains and stirred seas.

Borrowing the baleful qi of the seven meridians to forge an iron-clad body; the Big Banner Gate's external technique; masters solidify bones and tendons, rendering weapons useless, possessing the might to oppose ten thousand.

Created by Yu Hongmei, combining the strengths of Shaolin and Tianshan sect's inner energy; overwhelmingly dominant, infinite power, yet it harbors boundless killing intent — only those with a heart like a clear mirror can perceive its true meaning.
Stepping through pavilions to tread the sea, walking reclined to soar through air; the footwork passed down by Tianya Haige embodies unrestrained elegance, uniquely scholarly in demeanor.
Footwork derived from the Eight Trigrams, flowing like coiling serpents—also called Coiling Body Eight Trigram Steps. Legend claims eight steps suffice to catch a cicada without disrupting posture.
Flowing like water, shifting like momentum; formless and unpredictable—this movement style resembles turbulent currents, elusive and fathomless. Its origins have become untraceable.
Tales tell of a goddess whose light lotus steps held ethereal grace and mystical subtlety.
Steps inspired by winter plum blossoms' cold fragrance, solitary yet profound—a rare and ingenious footwork art in the martial world.
This technique’s source is lost to time. It mimics the pangolin's form—diving, rolling, striking enemies unprepared, evading the unevadable.
Ascending to azure skies via cloud ladders; peering at drifting mist—can enlightenment’s path be glimpsed?
"Ten paces slay one foe; a thousand miles leave no trace." Phantoms and spirits tread bloodied paths in sinister steps.
Soaring swallow flight—body and step united—piercing clouds with grace, containing myriad variations.
Long pavilions, ancient roads; homeland’s bright moon fades far away. With none returning, how shall this sorrow be written?
Ethereal tread on trembling waves, silk socks dusted, swirling like snow—dancing like immortal steeds.
Still as silver pythons barring mountains; swift as golden boas parting rivers. Five Sacred Cult's unique maneuvering art diverges sharply from Central Plains techniques.
Mystical birds depart, wild geese herald mid-autumn; this movement flows like wind, powerful as soaring rocs—free yet ever composed.
External "solid bridge, solid horse" stance, embodying earth-shaking steps that resound with might.
To cultivate martial arts is to swim upstream—once your form arrives, why not strike against the current?
Light as gale-swept shadows, fierce as tigers pacing mountains. Steady yet mutable, solid yet fluid—maneuvering in tight spaces or racing faster than galloping steeds.
Yu Hongmei's unique footwork—uncanny and elusive, stepping on snow without traces, crossing water without ripples.
Wolf fang tearing—ferocious and bone-deep—yet lacking technical finesse.
Venomous fang tearing—imbued with deadly poison—agony runs marrow-deep, yet devoid of technique.
The swift leaping technique of the martial world, with feet planted like a tripod, propels the user upward in a mighty leap.
